items.summary: Modular networks, such as critical infrastructures, are often built from distinct, densely connected modules (e.g. cities) that are sparsely interconnected. When such networks are gradually and randomly disrupted under a percolation process, they undergo two critical phase transitions. The first transition occurs when modules become isolated from one another, while the second corresponds to the collapse of the entire network, including the internal connectivity of the modules. Here, we study these phase transitions in modular multiplex networks and compare them with those observed in single-layer modular networks. We focus on models in which the modules are arranged and connected either as a short-range two-dimensional square lattice or as a long-range random regular (RR) network. We show here that these systems exhibit diverse transition behaviors, with some transitions occurring continuously and others abruptly; notably, one realistic model display two distinct abrupt transitions in the same system. By tuning the range of the inter-module connectivity between these two limits, we further show that the order of the spatial transition changes gradually from continuous to abrupt. For the modular RR multiplex, we further characterize the spatial transition through its scaling behavior, revealing signatures of a mixed-order phase transition. In addition, we analytically determine the critical threshold at which modules become disconnected. Our results highlight the crucial role of modular organization and the critical role of interdependence in shaping network vulnerabilities under failures.

items.title: From Topological Order to Mixed-State Phases: A Ground-State Probe of Fractionalized Excitations
authors: Yunlong Zang, Yu-Bin Li and Shenghan Jiang
items.summary: How do we detect topological phases from a single ground state? Entanglement entropy and spectrum have long been the standard tools—but the reduced density matrix (RDM) itself contains far more information. We show that the RDM of a 2D topologically ordered system, expressed at the entanglement cut, realizes a 1D mixed-state phase. For the toric code phase, it is a 1D strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB) phase, where deconfinement of anyons manifests as the short-range correlation of both charge and domain-wall in the RDM. The bulk e–m duality translates into a Kramers–Wannier self-duality of the SW-SSB phase. Extending the framework to gapped spin liquids, the global spin-rotation symmetry manifests as an additional weak symmetry for the 1D RDM. Spin-1/2 spinons result in a cusp on the disorder parameter of spin-rotation at θ = π, providing a direct, ground-state signature of symmetry fractionalization. We verify this prediction analytically using the matrix product density operator formalism and numerically for the kagome-lattice resonating valence bond state. The proposed observable requires only a single ground-state wavefunction, making it amenable to quantum simulation platforms.

items.title: Symmetry-Enforced Single-Pair Charge-Two Triple-Point Semimetals
authors: Hui-Jing Zheng, Ke-Xin Pang, Yun-Yun Bai, Yan Gao and Zhong-Yi Lu
items.summary: The Nielsen–Ninomiya theorem mandates that the net chiral charge of topological nodes in a crystal’s Brillouin zone must vanish, requiring them to appear in pairs. While realizing the absolute minimum of a single pair of topological nodes has been achieved for Weyl semimetals, hosting the minimal configuration of chiral charge-two (|C| = 2) triple-degenerate points (C-2 TPs) in a realistic electronic material remains an open challenge. By combining little-group constraints with both possible two-node orbit structures across all 1651 magnetic space groups (MSGs), we identify 21 MSGs without spin–orbit coupling (SOC) and 3 MSGs with SOC that are compatible with an isolated single pair of C-2 TPs. Guided by these symmetry criteria, we predict that the cubic boron allotrope P23-B36 acts as a premier electronic platform for this exotic phase. Owing to the negligible SOC of light boron atoms, the system behaves as a spinless semimetal, where the three crossing bands form exactly two symmetry-enforced C-2 TPs at the high-symmetry points Γ and R with chiralities C = +2 and C = 2, respectively. First-principles calculations reveal maximally extended double Fermi arcs on both the (001) and (110) surfaces, providing a distinct spectroscopic fingerprint for experimental detection. Our work establishes a rigorous symmetry-guided design framework for minimal multifold semimetals and identifies an elemental platform for exploring their intrinsic quantum transport phenomena.

They find that lighter fluxoniums are less susceptible to these transitions than heavier counterparts, and trace this to three key mechanisms. These results provide a path toward optimizing fluxonium design for fast, high-fidelity readout.

The common vortex size also allows distinct OAM states to overlap and interfere on the same ring, producing programmable petal-like pressure patterns. These capabilities could facilitate acoustic multiplexing and detection, and structured-wave sensing and particle manipulation.

This study shows that applying four non-coplanar bias fields breaks this deadlock, revealing both quantities at once. This self-calibration could enable nanodiamond sensing in complex environments such as living cells and aqueous solutions, where precalibrating the sensor is not an option.

items.title: Stacking-Order-Dependent Electronic Properties of MoTe 2 /WSe 2 Moiré Bilayers
authors: Zhongdong Han, Wenjin Zhao, Eegene Clara Chung, Chia-Hao Lee, Zui Tao, Zhengchao Xia, Yichi Zhang, Yiyu Xia, Jekwan Lee, Bowen Shen, Ariana Ray, Yu-Tsun Shao, Tingxin Li, Shengwei Jiang, Yihang Zeng, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, David A. Muller, Kin Fai Mak, and Jie Shan
items.summary: Abstract Transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) moiré bilayers have realized a wide range of strongly correlated and topological phenomena. The physics in these materials is often sensitive to the interlayer stacking order. Polarization-resolved optical second harmonic generation (SHG) is the most used technique for stacking order characterization but unverified for most heterobilayers. Here we calibrate the optical SHG for angle-aligned MoTe 2 /WSe 2 bilayers by the scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM). We directly compare the transport and magnetic properties and the electronic phase diagram for two distinct stacking orders. With the calibrated stacking order assignment, we clarify the interpretation of earlier results, including the nature of the Chern insulator, mechanism of an electric-field-tuned metal–insulator transition at half band filling, and the Kondo lattice physics. Our work provides a consistent picture of the relation between the stacking order and the electronic properties of MoTe 2 /WSe 2 moiré bilayers.

items.title: Giant Resistance Switching Ratio Exceeding 10 6 through a Reversible 2D–3D Structural Phase Transition in Nonequilibrium (Pb 1– x Sn x )Se Thin Films
authors: Naoto Hoshi, Sota Abe, Sangjin Choi, Kota Hanzawa, Hiroto Arima, Jun-ichi Yamaura, Shogo Hatayama, Hidenori Hiramatsu, Toshio Kamiya, and Takayoshi Katase
items.summary: Abstract Control and switching of electrical resistance in semiconductors are important for high-performance electronic devices. Here, we realize giant resistance switching in nonequilibrium (Pb 1– x Sn x )Se films through a reversible structural transition between three-dimensional (3D) rock-salt (RS)-type and two-dimensional (2D) GeS-type phases. The solid-solution films were fabricated by reactive solid-phase epitaxy of SnSe/PbSe bilayers followed by rapid thermal quenching. Se-flux annealing of the PbSe template suppressed Pb precipitation, enabling chemically homogeneous, single-phase nonequilibrium RS-type films up to x = 0.58. Increasing the Sn content from x = 0.43 to 0.58 systematically increased the 2D–3D structural transition temperature and enhanced the resistance switching ratio to 4.9 × 10 6 , far exceeding those of representative transition-metal oxide thin films (∼10 2 –10 4 ). The giant resistance switching originates from the nearly complete transformation (∼98%) of the conductive 3D phase into the high-resistance 2D phase. These results establish crystal-dimensionality switching as a promising new mechanism for high-performance electronic switching devices.

items.title: Emergent single-species non-reciprocity from bistable chemical dynamics
items.summary: Metson and Golestanian describe a new class of intelligent active matter systems in which non-reciprocal interactions emerge spontaneously in a homogeneous single-species, non-equilibrium chemically active suspension of microreactors. The work is based on a conceptual paradigm of emergent symmetries and their associated spontaneous symmetry breaking. The proposed framework gives a strong perspective of how lifelike traits of signaling, sensing, and propulsion can spontaneously and effortlessly emerge in such systems.

items.title: Synthetic data training for machine-learning-assisted ARPES experiments
authors: Meng Xing Na, Chris Zhou, Sydney K.Y. Dufresne, Matteo Michiardi, Andrea Damascelli
items.summary: Training artificial intelligence (AI) for experimental science usually requires huge collections of labeled data, which many techniques, such as angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), simply do not have. Na et al. show that synthetic ARPES data can fill the gap. They develop a high-fidelity ARPES simulator, aurelia, and train an AI model capable of judging the quality of real measurement data and of picking up the best spot to measure on the sample surface more precisely than a conventional analysis, highlighting the potential of AI-assisted experiments.

items.title: Threefold-Symmetric Te Nanoparticles for Stabilizing Zinc Metal Anodes
authors: Jiawei Su, ChangChun Fan, Zhuoyuan Li, Weiguang Lan, Guoming Lin, Wenhui Wang, and Mingjie Liu
items.summary: Abstract Uncontrolled Zn nucleation and growth at the electrode–electrolyte interface limit the reversibility and lifetime of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Nanoparticle (NP)-based anode protective layers are widely used to regulate Zn deposition, yet precise control over the exposed zincophilic facets of individual NPs remains challenging. Here, we show a facet-geometry engineering strategy based on threefold-symmetric Te nanoparticles (TF–Te NPs) to modulate Zn plating/stripping during cycling. The TF–Te NPs present a high density of zincophilic facets, while their threefold symmetric geometry spatially clusters nucleation sites within nanoscale proximity, promoting uniform Zn deposition and accelerating interfacial kinetics. As a result, TF–Te NP-modified Zn anodes exhibit reduced nucleation overpotentials, improved rate capability, and enhanced cycling stability. Our work establishes a direct link between NP geometry, facet-dependent zincophilicity, and Zn deposition behavior, offering a strategy for engineering NP protective layers across a broad range of aqueous batteries.
